description:
Every semantic mutation re-resolves each document reference in the repository through up to three fresh git subprocesses, so mutation latency scales with the repository's document-reference count rather than with the size of the change. At this repository's size a dependency add costs 3.2 s, of which 2.3 s is process spawning; in an adopter repository with 1497 document references a single idempotent label update costs 18 s.

## Background

Repository image capture backs `@/inv/derived-state-coherence`: a mutation derives its coupled materializations from one final repository view, so the capture must witness every document reference that view depends on. Capture builds that evidence one reference at a time. `capture_capability_image` iterates the pinned set and calls `inspect_pinned_target` per entry (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:888-894`). That call spawns `git rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit}` to resolve the revision (`crates/jit/src/storage/git_revision.rs:144`), `git ls-tree` to classify one path (`crates/jit/src/storage/git_revision.rs:208`), and, when the target is a file, `git cat-file blob` to read its content for the content identity (`crates/jit/src/storage/git_revision.rs:239`).

None of the spawns is amortized across the set. Unpinned references all carry one revision (`UNPINNED_REVISION = "HEAD"`, `crates/jit/src/document/reference.rs:40`), so for them the revision half is a single identical query repeated once per reference; pinned references repeat each of their few distinct revisions the same way. The path half asks git for one tree entry at a time where one listing answers every entry at once, and the content half starts one process per blob where one long-lived batch reader serves them all.

The per-reference cost is then multiplied by the capture count. A dependency add captures twice, once in preflight and once in the attempt (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:259-310`); issue creation captures three times.

Measured on this repository at 1071 issues and 445 unpinned document references:

| operation | git processes | wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dependency add | 1575 | 3209 ms |
| issue create | 2361 | 3164 ms |
| whole-repository validate | 789 | 1087 ms |
| any read operation | 3 | 27-36 ms |

Latency is linear in two independent terms: 0.18 ms per issue, and 4.5 ms per document reference. The second dominates. Removing the document references from those same 1071 issues drops a dependency add to 203 ms, a 15.8x difference at unchanged issue count, which isolates the reference term as the cause.

An adopter repository confirms the shape at larger scale and adds the two terms this repository under-exercises. At 864 issues, one idempotent label update ran 18.2 s wall (6.3 s user, 10.0 s system) and spawned 8988 git processes: 2994 each of `rev-parse --verify`, `ls-tree`, and `cat-file blob`. That is 1497 distinct references, most of them files, across 42 distinct revisions, captured twice. Because the whole capture runs under the repository bootstrap lock, concurrent mutations and gate evaluations in that repository time out on the lock after 5 s, which raised observed per-update latency to 25-50 s.

Reads are unaffected and stay flat. The defect is confined to the capture path that mutations and whole-repository validation share.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One capture resolves every distinct revision among its N references with a number of git processes independent of both N and the distinct-revision count whenever every revision resolves, and re-resolves each revision per capture so a revision that moves between captures is observed.
- [hard] REQ-02: Classifying N document paths at one revision, and reading the content of the file targets among them, issues a number of git processes independent of N.
- [hard] REQ-03: Tree classification and content reads for a resolved commit-and-path pair run at most once while the pair remains in the most recent capture, so repeating a capture over unchanged revisions issues only the revision-resolution process; cached evidence is keyed by resolved commit, never by revision name, and retains only pairs used by the most recent capture that pins any document reference, so a capture pinning nothing neither spawns a git process nor evicts cached evidence.
- [hard] REQ-04: A dependency add over 1071 issues and 445 unpinned document references spawns fewer than 20 git processes and completes in under 1000 ms, evidenced by a benchmark artifact committed under the issue and linked to it.
- [hard] REQ-05: Pinned-document evidence is unchanged for every target class: resolved commit, object id, target kind, content identity, and unavailable reason match what per-reference resolution produces today for a present file, an executable file, a directory, an unsupported entry, a path missing from the commit, and an unresolvable revision.
- [hard] REQ-06: Core commands still work with git absent, and a reference whose revision cannot be resolved still records its unavailable reason rather than failing the command.
- [hard] REQ-07: Regression coverage fails if per-reference or per-revision resolution processes, per-path tree classification, per-blob content reads, or repeated classification and reads across captures over unchanged commits are reintroduced.
- [hard] REQ-08: A mutation over a repository whose document references span several distinct pinned revisions, mostly file targets, spawns git processes bounded by a constant plus a small multiple of the distinct-revision count, independent of the reference count, evidenced in the same benchmark artifact.

## Notes

The measurements for this repository come from synthetic repositories subsampled from it, varying issue count and document-reference count independently, timed on tmpfs. Timings on tmpfs and on disk agree to within 4%, which establishes the cost as process spawning rather than storage I/O. A CPU profile attributes the remainder to `CaptureSpec::validate`, path parsing, and SHA-256 content hashing, all of which stay linear in reference count and are out of scope here.

Scaling stays linear after the fix, so the reference term governs how the tracker ages: at roughly twice the current size an unfixed mutation costs about 6 s.

Evidence caching is keyed by resolved commit rather than scoped to a command because a long-lived server process shares one storage instance across requests: a cache keyed by revision name would serve a stale `HEAD` indefinitely, while commit-keyed tree entries and blobs are immutable.

`@/charter/D-4` keeps git optional for core commands, which bounds the fix: batching may not turn an absent or failing git into a hard error on a path that tolerates it today.
title: Every mutation spawns up to three git processes per document reference
